input.quote: 3. that is brought by a Services Recipient and is related, directly or indirectly, to the Services; or
input.rationale: Section 8.1 gives us a genuine IBM IP indemnity (patent, trademark, copyright, trade secret) covering Materials and Base Components, with the usual exclusions (our inputs, our modifications, combinations, non-IBM items) and remedies (continue use, modify, replace, credit up to 12 months' charges), and it is carved out of IBM's liability cap under Section 9.1(a) — so the vendor-side IP indemnity sits at or above the fallback and we are not redlining it (the preferred breach-of-law, data-breach and wilful-misconduct limbs are absent, which we note but do not flag). The failure is on the other side of the bargain: Section 8.2(a)(3) makes us indemnify IBM for any third-party claim brought by a Services Recipient "related, directly or indirectly, to the Services" — an open-ended, uncapped indemnity (Section 9.2(a) excludes it from our cap) for IBM's own Services, which is walk-away territory under this rule; the partial relief in 8.2(c) for IBM's misconduct does not cure it. Minimal fix: narrow that limb to our breach of applicable law, leaving the Content/AUP and Customer Components limbs intact so our indemnity matches the preferred position.

ops.oldText: 3. that is brought by a Services Recipient and is related, directly or indirectly, to the Services; or
ops.newText: 3. that arises out of Customer's breach of applicable law; or

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We narrowed our indemnity in Section 8.2(a)(3) so that we do not indemnify IBM, without limitation of liability, for any claim by a Services Recipient relating to IBM's own Services; our playbook limits the customer indemnity to Customer-provided Content and our breach of applicable law. We are content for IBM's IP indemnity in Section 8.1 to stand as drafted.
proposal.summary: Limit Customer's indemnity to Customer Content and Customer's breach of law by removing the open-ended Services Recipient limb.
